title: Absence norms without violations are never considered; the certified ones match a shuffled null
evidence:
Pairs (A,B) are only created `for (const B of targets)`, where targets are modules reached by at least one file in A (arch.mjs:54). A module that has never crossed a boundary therefore never becomes a candidate. The null is a flat coin: `data += nv*log2(kt(...)*2)` (arch.mjs:99), and vacuity is patched with `outsideShare(n) >= 0.1` (:131).

Synthetic check (scratchpad arch.mjs): domain 0/20 reach infra while app 18/20 and api 19/20 do. Output: only `app->infra true`, `api->infra true` and `util->infra false 19/20` (util has 1 violation). The perfectly held domain boundary is absent.

Permutation check (perm.mjs, out-edge sets shuffled across files so no real structure remains, 20 runs):
- Yggdrasil: real certifies 2 absence norms, the null 2.5 per run.
- Grain: real 1, the null 3.5.

The real Yggdrasil norms are `.yggdrasil/aspects -/-> core 324/325` (YAML/markdown files that cannot import anything), `tests -/-> utils 1174/1199` (bits 1008, purely n under a 50/50 null) and `relations -/-> core`, which the hand graph explicitly allows (propose-types.mjs:318).

A contrast-null prototype (arch3.mjs) over files that have at least one out-edge finds zero-violation boundaries on Yggdrasil: `io -/-> core 0/22 vs 43.5% elsewhere, 8.2 bits` and `core -/-> cli 0/66 vs 12.1%`. Hand aspects of exactly this shape exist: events-reader-boundary ("NO file under source/cli/src/core/** may import it") and no-child-process.

mine() has the same gap at scope level: a local absence speaks only if the thing is used by ≥30% of the partition (mine.mjs:432), so "core never imports node:child_process" dies when child_process is rare. The 097 study named the lost bet: "Hand-written rules are negative and specific because a decision was made".
proposal:
Replace the flat null with a two-population contrast, the same cell the bridge and obligations already use.

1. Condition on capability: n_A = files in A with at least one resolved out-edge.
2. Take k_O / n_O = the reach-B rate over capable files outside A and outside B.
3. Candidate universe: every (A,B) with k_O ≥ minRaw, including k_A = 0. The index cost is ⌈log2 C⌉ over that universe.
4. Gain = Σ_v n_v·log2(KT_A(v) / p_O(v)) − ½·log2 n_A − idxCost. For a perfect absence this is ≈ n_A·log2(1/(1−p_O)) − O(1). Example: n=22, p_O=0.435 gives ≈18 bits before costs.
5. Speak when gain > 0 and the posterior (n_A−k_A+½)/(n_A+1) ≥ 1−1/λ.

This deletes the 0.1 and 0.3 floors. Apply the same contrast to mine()'s local boolean-absence cells: code the directory's outcome at the out-of-directory rate, not at the partition rate plus a 30% floor. Render zero-violation contrasts as `deny` candidates carrying "0 of n, vs p_O elsewhere".

Cost: about 60 lines in arch.mjs plus the mine() absence filter, and one extra module×module sweep that is already O(modules × targets).

How we'd know:
- (a) The permutation run certifies ≈0 absence norms, below the real count.
- (b) The .yggdrasil/aspects and tests->utils vacuous norms disappear.
- (c) Re-run 097's B1 bar restricted to negative hand rules (import fences) on Yggdrasil and the four oracles, then count hand deny/fence rules whose module pair appears as a certified zero-violation contrast. Today that count is 0 by construction.

title: Sub-gate lattice feeds advisory rules on raw share; most rows fail Grain's own objective
evidence:
`subGate = rows.filter(r => !r.isNorm && r.n >= MIN_SUPPORT && r.share >= SUPERMAJORITY && r.share < LAMBDA_BOUND)` (propose-lattice.mjs:89). There is no bits test. The index cost is per partition (`cells.size`, :47), unlike the repo-wide rule §9.4a. The absence floor here is 0.2 (:68), against mine()'s 0.1 and 0.3. The STRUCT_PID vacuity contrast that mine() applies is not applied either.

Measured with lat.mjs, which calls the engine's own partitionLattice on the cached models. The Beta bound is the 5% lower quantile of Beta(k+½, n−k+½).

| | Band rows | bits ≤ 0 | 95% lower bound ≥ 2/3 | top row |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grain | 485 | 321 (66%) | 140 (29%) | `_repo _all:case auto.has:member_expression 358/410` (describes the language) |
| Yggdrasil | 669 | 387 (58%) | 234 (35%) | |

These rows become `advisory` after a drill (propose-status.mjs:237). In Grain's self-proposal, 22 advisory rules came from them (results.md row 104/107). Result 101 already recorded the consequence: precision 0.091 on held-out rows, and "14 of 20 rows are not rules at all — minority usage read as a negative rule".
proposal:
Gate the band with the objective, not with share.

1. Require bits_contrast > 0, using the role-vs-partition contrast for role cells and GM-1's contrast for `_all` absences, with one repo-wide idxCost shared with mine()'s `Crepo`.
2. Require the Beta(k+½, n−k+½) lower 5% quantile ≥ 2/3. Keep the upper band edge as "posterior mean < 1−1/λ".
3. Apply STRUCT_PID's contrast-only rule.
4. Rank the per-partition reading cap (SUBGATE_PER_PARTITION) by bits, not by share.

On today's numbers this cuts the band to at most 140 and 234 rows before rendering, and removes the language-describing rows.

Cost: about 30 lines, no new constant (the Beta quantile is the λ-style posterior already in use).

How we'd know: re-run 101's bar-2 panel sample and the Grain and Yggdrasil self-proposals. Advisory precision on the held-out rows should rise from 0.091, and the count of "not a rule" rows in the 20-row sample should drop from 14. Drill false alarms must stay at 0.

title: The repair signal (was a departure later fixed?) is computed but unreachable and unused
evidence:
`calibrate` is the only place Grain measures whether departures from a norm get repaired, which is how an enforced decision shows up in history. It is never reached in practice:
- It needs history older than 365 absolute days (`if (H.firstTs > split)`, weights.mjs:161). The message there says 'history<2x horizon', but the code checks 1x.
- It needs ≥12 events and decodes values only for 5 predicate families (`valOf`: nameshape, first1, ret, deco:@, extends). Imports and calls, where hand fences live, are never decoded.

Grain's own model: 238 facts, 0 with calibration available (all 'history<2x horizon'), 0 with `rejected`, 0 with `cost`, 0 nucleating.

The outputs are not consumed where rules are tiered either: `finalStatus = origin === 'certified-convention' ? 'enforced' : 'advisory'` (propose-status.mjs:237). No propose-*.mjs file reads `calib`, `rejected`, `trend` or `cost`.

Meanwhile 097 concluded that law is decided, not observed as a majority. The observable trace of a decision is that departures are repaired or reverted, which is exactly what these functions measure.
proposal:
Turn repair into a certified per-fact signal and use it in tiering.

1. Store a bounded value vector per vev event for every mined pid family. Imports: the top-K vocabulary ids a file carries, as a bitset. This replaces the 5-family `valOf`.
2. For each certified fact, gather departure events D (a scope moves exp→v, or is born with v, after the cut).
3. Label d ∈ D repaired if the scope returns to exp, or is deleted, within the rest of history.
4. Base rate r0 = the share of conformers whose value leaves and returns within the same span (ordinary churn).
5. Certify "enforced in practice" when Σ_v n_v·log2(KT_D(v)/r0(v)) − ½·log2|D| − log2(C_facts) > 0 and the KT predictive P(repaired) ≥ 1−1/λ.
6. Cut the history by commit index, not days: the first 70% of commits train, the last 30% are the events. The fingerprint lab already uses this rule (results.md 149).
7. Merge `rejectedValues` into the same cell as the "tried and reverted" arm.

In propose:
- certified + repaired-in-practice → enforced candidate;
- certified with departures that are never repaired → advisory ("habit, nobody fixes it");
- sub-gate + repaired → a promotion candidate with the evidence line "k of n departures were fixed".

Cost: history cache grows (one bitset per value event, roughly +10-20% of history.json by estimate), plus about 150 lines.

How we'd know: on Yggdrasil and the four hand oracles, compute the AUC with which the repair statistic separates mined facts matching a hand deterministic aspect's identifier from those that don't. Also check whether B1 in 097 (0/20 reproduced) moves once tiering uses repair.
effort: L (3-5 days incl. cache format bump)

Grain's model shows 238/238 facts 'history<2x horizon' and 0 with rejected/cost/nucleating. No propose*.mjs reads calib/rejected/trend/cost (grep). title: Time axis in wall-clock days disables drift and nucleation on young, fast repositories
where: Grain plugins/grain/engine/weights.mjs:64-65, :91, :102, :117; config.mjs trendWinDays:90, calibHorizonDays:365; learn.mjs:417 (180 days)
proposal:
Replace the trend and nucleation detector with an MDL change point on the arrival (birth) sequence.

1. Order a fact's instances by birth, i = 1..n, with x_i = 1 if the instance carries exp.
2. L1 = −log2 KT_seq(x_1..n), the true sequential KT code.
3. L2(τ) = −log2 KT_seq(x_1..τ) − log2 KT_seq(x_τ+1..n) + log2(n−1), paying for τ.
4. A regime change is certified iff L1 − min_τ L2(τ) − log2(C_facts) > 0.
5. Then act on the recent segment's KT predictive:
   - if P(exp | post-τ) < 1−1/λ, the fact stops accusing births after τ (a fading convention);
   - if some v ≠ exp has P(v | post-τ) ≥ 1−1/λ, report nucleation of v.

This needs no windows, no slope and no author count, is indexed by commit order, and works at any pace. It reads only `H.lc` first-seen timestamps and `vev`, both already stored. Use commit-index quantiles for the 180-day `fresh` count as well.

Cost: about 80 lines, O(n) per fact with prefix counts.

How we'd know:
- (a) On Grain and on the agent-authored segments of Yggdrasil, count change points found, then spot-check by reading the commits around τ.
- (b) Take a corpus repo with a known migration (e.g. express's move to async handlers, or nest decorator changes) and check that τ lands within a few commits of the migration.
- (c) The mutation harness's false-fire count stays at 0.

Grain's model has 19 trend facts, each with a single window (e.g. [{share:1,n:125}]), and 0 nucleating. Grain's first commit is 2026-08-24 and Yggdrasil started in May 2026, so nucleation can never fire on any family repo. mathematics.md:24 says drift/nucleation reads 'the arrival process of a rule's instances', which the windowed OLS does not do. title: Agent provenance ignores Co-Authored-By trailers, so agent weighting is blind in the family's own repositories
where: Grain plugins/grain/engine/history.mjs:268, :283; config.mjs AGENT_AUTHOR_RE; weights.mjs:38-42; learn.mjs:254; report.mjs:443
evidence:
The git log format reads only `%an <%ae>` and `%s` (history.mjs:268). `agent: AGENT_AUTHOR_RE.test(p[2])` checks the author string only (:283). No commit body or trailers are read.

Counted with `git show -s --format=%B` per commit:
- Grain: 229 of 229 commits authored "Krzysztof Dudek" carry `Co-Authored-By: Claude`.
- Yggdrasil: 1339 of 1572 commits under Krzysztof's name carry an agent trailer (85%), and only 11 are authored "Claude".

All of these count as human. As a result:
- the provenance weight (agentBase 0.15 promoted over 180 days, weights.mjs:40-41) never applies;
- the "agent-authored share … ALARM" line (report.mjs:443, alarm at 0.85) under-reports on exactly the repository where the true share is about 0.85;
- exemplars are labelled "human-authored" (learn.mjs:254) when they are not.

This matters for the thesis: agent-written code is the base-rate population Grain is meant to discount.
proposal:
Add `%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly,separator=%x1f)` to the log format. Set agent = AGENT_AUTHOR_RE matches the author OR any co-author. Keep a three-valued provenance (human, agent, pair) so weighting can treat pair-authored code separately. Pair could start at the agent weight, since the agent typed it and the human approved it.

This bumps HIST_V, so the next run rebuilds history.

Cost: about 15 lines plus a history rebuild.

How we'd know:
- Yggdrasil's agent-share line moves from about 0 to about 0.8, and the ALARM fires.
- Re-run the 4-oracle reconstruction and the mutation harness. The expectation is no regression, with some conventions losing weight where agent code dominated.
- Count how many certified facts on Yggdrasil owe their certification to trailer-agent code: these are the claims whose "established" status is currently overstated.

title: The deviation "cost" is not normalised for exposure, yet the output wording is causal
evidence:
`fixOutcome` is binary: `L.fix > 0 ? 'has_fix' : 'no_fix'` (learn.mjs:111). `L.fix` is incremented only when a fix commit modifies the scope (history.mjs:599), so the label measures exposure.

On Grain's history (8193 scopes), P(fix>0) by number of modifications:

| mods | P(fix>0) |
|---|---|
| 0 | 0.000 |
| 1-2 | 0.132 |
| 3-5 | 0.480 |
| 6+ | 0.529 |

Deviants that are simply edited more (older code, hot files) will certify as "costly".

The output is causal: "deviants get fixes N× more often" (mine.mjs:708) and "costs N× more fixes when deviated from" (report-facts.mjs:217). The fingerprint lab already found that the fix label measures exposure and size, not defect (results.md 150, 152, 157: "the fix label sees exposure, not protection").
proposal:
Code fix events per modification, not per scope.

1. For deviants D and the whole population P, count modification events: fix_D = Σ L.fix and m_D = Σ L.mods, and likewise fix_P and m_P.
2. Contrast the binomial per-modification rate: gain = fix_D·log2(KT_D(fix)/q_P) + (m_D−fix_D)·log2(KT_D(plain)/(1−q_P)) − ½·log2 m_D − idxCostD, where q_P = fix_P/m_P.
3. Keep the λ bound on the claimed direction.
4. For a stronger version, stratify by scope size (lines), since size dominated every fingerprint model: sum per-stratum codelengths with stratum-specific q, in the style of Mantel-Haenszel.

Reword as an association: "edits to deviants were fix commits X× as often (k of m edits vs q)". Never "costs".

Cost: about 40 lines, and no new fields (mods and fix already exist in `H.lc`).

How we'd know: across the corpus, compare the number of `cost` claims before and after. Hand-check 10 surviving claims to confirm the deviants are not just the hottest scopes. The popularity-matched control from 153 should show no residual lift if the effect was exposure.

'has_fix' : 'no_fix'`, and history.mjs:597-599 increments fix only on a modification, so the label is exposure-confounded exactly as results.md 157 found ('exposure, not protection'). Grain's own model has 0 cost claims, so the impact is on the corpus, not the family repos. The per-modification rate is a sound, cheap fix. The wording change to association should ship regardless.

title: Co-change gate uses the max of both directions and no base-rate contrast, contradicting the λ loss
evidence:
`if (Math.max(confAB, confBA) < minConf) continue;` (completeness.mjs:57). The display denominator is "whichever direction cleared the bar" (:60).

Reproduction (scratchpad cc.mjs), with pair {hub lib/response.js commitsA=392, test commitsB=10, sup=8}: `cochangeData(model, ['lib/response.js'])` returns `test/res.attachment.js` with `commits:10`, rendered "co-changed in 8/10 commits" (completeness.mjs:220). The same happens under the stricter 0.75 multi-file gate. The forward probability the editor cares about is P(test | hub) = 8/392 ≈ 2%, which fails λ=8 by about 40×.

The gates are raw confidences (0.75, 1/3 and support 8), not the KT contrast against the partner's base rate used by obligations and the bridge. history.mjs:704 says consumers should gate directionally ("editing `a` names `b` iff sup/commitsA ≥ minConf"), and the consumer does the opposite.

The recorded consequences:
- "raw co-change recall@3 (0.285) loses to the null '3 hottest recently-changed files' (0.336)" (completeness.mjs:41-43);
- 153 showed "the partner's lift over a random neighbour is entirely its popularity".
proposal:
Use the obligation cell for co-change.

1. For editing a, code b's touched/untouched outcome over the commitsA commits at KT(sup/commitsA) vs b's base rate commitsB/N.
2. Gain = sup·log2(KT(t)/p_b) + (commitsA−sup)·log2(KT(¬t)/(1−p_b)) − ½·log2 commitsA − log2(#pairs).
3. Speak iff gain > 0 and the forward posterior (sup+½)/(commitsA+1) ≥ 1−1/λ, the same λ used everywhere else. Allow a documented softer display bound for single-file hints only if it is measured.
4. The reverse direction (b→a) is spoken only when b is the file being edited.

This deletes cochangeMinConf and both 1/3 floors, and cochangeMinSup becomes a pure compute guard.

Cost: about 40 lines, plus re-running `selftest --where` and `--obligation`.

How we'd know:
- recall@3 / precision@1 against the null-hot baseline on the 20-repo obligations-design set (today 0.285 vs 0.336);
- the 153 popularity-matched control repeated on contrast-certified partners;
- hub files stop naming low-probability partners (on express, lib/response.js).

title: Value concordance's 50/50 null certifies schema furniture: 4 of 4 certified norms are YAML schema keys
evidence:
`data += nv * Math.log2(kt(counts, KV, v, neff) * 2)` (learn.mjs:806) is a flat coin, justified in mathematics.md as "there is no natural per-file prior for 'carries the whole set'".

Every certified norm in the two cached models:

| Repo | Container | Members | Carriers | bits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grain | `$.scope` | per/file | 56/56 | 40.4 |
| Grain | `$` | description/name | 175/177 | 145.4 |
| Yggdrasil | `$.scope` | per/file | 80/85 | 42.3 |
| Yggdrasil | `$.relations` | target/uses | 151/153 | 121.9 |

All four are keys the yg-aspect.yaml or node schema requires, so they co-occur by schema, not by choice. validation.md already found this family had certified duplicates before its container fix.
proposal:
There is a natural null: independence of members given their marginals.

1. Among files that declare the container, let p_j = the share carrying member j.
2. Under independence, P(full | qualifies) = Π_j p_j / P(≥t members), with the denominator computed exactly from the Poisson-binomial over the p_j.
3. Code the complete/incomplete outcome at KT vs that rate, with the same BIC, idxCostV and λ bound.

Members that are individually ubiquitous (p_j ≈ 1) predict completeness on their own, so gain ≈ 0 and nothing is certified. Real concordance, where members are individually optional but travel together, still compresses. Near-carriers (m−1) keep their meaning as residuals.

Cost: about 30 lines, O(m) per container.

How we'd know: the 4 schema norms stop certifying. On the corpus repos that had 3-4 distinct norms each (validation.md), inspect what survives. Enum/switch sets in code should dominate the survivors, and data-grammar schema keys should vanish.

The independence null (Poisson-binomial) is the correct fix and is cheap.

title: Multiple comparisons are paid per family with no repo-wide accounting or empirical null check
where: Grain plugins/grain/engine/learn.mjs:172, :562, :776; arch.mjs:89; commit-log.mjs:34, :146; obligations.mjs:108; propose-lattice.mjs:47 (per partition); spectrum.mjs:101; docs/mathematics.md:12-14
evidence:
mathematics.md: "an index cost charges for the choice of which cell speaks at all, so multiple comparisons are paid for inside the objective".

In code, at least 7 families each compute their own ⌈log2 C_f⌉: conventions, deviation cost, value norms, architecture norms, language bridge, change archetypes and obligations. The lattice pays per partition, and spectrum per call.

By the no-hypercompression inequality, P(a null cell gains ≥ k bits) ≤ 2^−k. With k = log2 C_f, each family's expected false certifications before λ are bounded by ≈1, so the repo-wide bound is ≈7, not ≈1. The bound also holds only for proper codes: the data term here is the end-of-sequence KT plug-in plus ½·log2 n, not the sequential KT code, so the slack is about 1 bit per cell.

No harness measures the realised null rate. The one run done here (perm.mjs) shows a family where the in-objective payment fails outright: shuffled edges certify 2.5 (Yggdrasil) and 3.5 (Grain) absence norms per run, at least as many as the real data.

title: Oracle score hides that the proposal is a near-perfect coarsening of the hand graph; add conditional-entropy partition metrics and relation projection
evidence: `grain oracle score tests/stress/oracles/yggdrasil --json` (run read-only): nodes recall n=402 hit=43 rate 0.107, precision n=83 rate 0.53; relations matchedNodes 44, acceptedPairs 39, `acceptedRelationsWithAnUnmappedEnd: 1259` of 1298, so 97% of the hand graph's relations are never scored. Prototype over the same record (proposal.json, accepted.json; 1416 files owned on both sides, deepest-node ownership). Against accepted leaves: H(P|A)=0.10 bits, H(A|P)=2.04 bits, inverse purity 0.968. So every accepted leaf sits inside one proposed node, and the hand graph is about 2 bits (~4x) finer. Sweeping accepted depth, VI is lowest at depth 4 (VI 1.52, ARI 0.662, NMI 0.878, purity 0.751). At depth 2 purity is 0.977. Relation projection: mapping each accepted node to the proposed node holding most of its files maps all 1298 accepted relations (0 unmappable); 194 collapse inside one proposed node, leaving 230 distinct pairs. Against the proposal's 216 pairs: overlap 205, recall 0.891, precision 0.949. This agrees with 093's file-pair numbers (0.894/0.998, docs/results.md row 093), which the node-matched score cannot see. results.md row 093 already names the confound: 'node mappings only 83/393 at J≥0.5, confounded by granularity'.
proposal: The math: treat both graphs as partitions of the tracked files. Report H(P|A) (the proposal over-splits), H(A|P) (the proposal under-splits), NMI and ARI, each at every depth of the accepted tree, plus the depth where VI is lowest. A proposal whose conditional entropy is near zero in one direction differs in granularity, not in cut. Relations are scored after projecting accepted edges onto the proposed partition (a graph homomorphism by file majority), so no relation drops out of the denominator. Data needed: nothing new; the oracle record already stores file index sets. Cost: about 150 pure lines in oracle.mjs, an additive `partition` and `relationsProjected` block in grain-oracle-score/1, and no schema break. How we would know: run it on all four oracles (express, grain, spring-petclinic, yggdrasil). Add a synthetic test: splitting every proposed node in two must raise H(P|A) and leave H(A|P) about the same, and merging must do the reverse. The measure has worked if the granularity confound in 093 turns into two numbers a maintainer can act on ('grain cuts at depth ~3-4 of your tree; finer nodes are yours to add').

title: Refusal-to-fix pairs in Yggdrasil's verdict history are free labelled data: drill pairs and evidence for turning prose rules into scripts, currently lost
where: Yggdrasil .yggdrasil/yg-events.llm.jsonl (committed), .yggdrasil/.yg-events.jsonl* (gitignored, rotated), yg-lock.nondeterministic.json; Grain (no reader); Horde skills/horde/scripts/retro.mjs:1-30
evidence: The committed yg-events.llm.jsonl holds 10,721 LLM verdicts from 2026-07-13 to 2026-09-25: 10,520 approved, 155 refused, 46 infra, 12 rules. There are 101 (rule, unit) pairs with a refusal; 96 were approved later on a changed hash, 5 never were. The time from refusal to approval has a median of 0.09 h (5.5 min) and a p90 of 0.32 h, so the fix is a small worktree edit that is almost never committed on its own. The committed events have no `reason` key (key set: aspectId, disposition, hash, judge, kind, promptRev, sha, source, tier, ts, unitKey, v, votes). The committed lock stores approvals only (0 occurrences of 'refused'). The local, gitignored .yg-events.jsonl.1 does carry `reason` text with file:line and backticked identifiers (69 refusals with a reason are still retained), but it rotates. Reviewer stability: 2080 (rule, unit, hash) keys were judged more than once, and 0 got different dispositions. Refusals by rule: what-why-next 56/2213, posix-paths-output 35/1035, test-deterministic 27/3027, diagnostic-logging 17/940. Horde's retro already sorts gate refusals into rule, taste or inexpressible with an LLM one-shot per mission (retro.mjs header). Grain grep for yg-events, drill-results and yg-lock: no hits.
proposal: Data prerequisite (Yggdrasil): on each refusal, keep the refused unit's content in a gitignored, content-addressed store (e.g. .yggdrasil/.refused/<hash>), and add `reason` to the local event (it is already there). Grain side: for each rule, pair every refused hash with the next approved hash of the same unit. Diff the two, then anti-unify the fix edits with the Plotkin LGG machinery Grain already uses for templates. An invariant edit (for example, output built with path.join replaced by toPosixPath) is a candidate deterministic check for a prose rule. It stands only if coding the rule's refusals through the candidate compresses: a KT cell of (flagged, refused) against the rule's base rate, the same λ=8 gate. Every refused/approved pair is also a ready-made failing/passing drill case pair for `yg drill add`. Cost: Yggdrasil ~1 day (blob write on refusal, gitignore line); Grain ~3-5 days (pairing, diff anti-unification, candidate rendering), with no LLM. How we would know: pre-register the bar before building. On Yggdrasil's posix-paths-output (35 refusals) and what-why-next (56), a leave-one-out derived check must catch ≥50% of held-out refusals with 0 false alarms on the ~3,000 approved hashes of those rules. Unlike law-loop 097, the labels here are the rule's own verdicts, so a miss is a real miss. Every script rule that replaces a prose rule also removes that rule's reviewer cost from CI.

title: Hidden coupling: node co-change measured against a lift null and grouped by channel finds real undeclared couplings that `grain advise` treats as data, not advice
where: Grain engine/grain-advise.mjs:123-208 (relationItems, mutual confidence ≥1/3), docs/reference.md 'The advice contract'; docs/results.md row 153
evidence: Prototype cochange.mjs imports Grain's readNodeGraph/declaredVia and runs over Yggdrasil HEAD: 505 nodes, 1775 relations, 1637 non-merge commits (1314 used: ≤50 files and touching ≥1 owned file). There are 312 node pairs co-changed ≥8 times; declaredVia gives 82 relation, 1 ancestor-relation, 2 containment, 227 none. Under advise's own rule (mutual confidence ≥1/3), 38 pairs pass and 10 are undeclared. With lift ≥4, 119 pass and 43 are undeclared: 23 code-code, 12 code-test, 8 test-test. The top undeclared pairs: cli/portal/contract ↔ cli/portal/frontend/views (11 co-commits of 13/15, lift 74); cli/knowledge ↔ docs/guides (84 co-commits, lift 4.0); cli/commands/advise ↔ cli/tests/unit/core/advise (lift 31.6). Channel check: 120 of 134 property names in portal/contract.ts (0.90) appear in templates/portal/js/views/**/*.js. For 16 random non-portal TS files with ≥10 fields the median share is 0.52 (max 0.72). The contract↔views coupling crosses TypeScript into browser JavaScript, where no import resolver can see it. The advice contract records the change-together side as 'data, not advice' after it named 2 pairs, both declared, on four hand graphs. Row 153 finds a co-change partner no more predictive than a popularity-matched file. Side note: the median share of a node's commits that stay inside that node is 0.00 over 117 nodes with ≥10 commits, so cohesion at leaf level says nothing on a graph this fine.
proposal: The math: replace the min-confidence floor with the test Grain already uses for the language bridge, a KT/λ likelihood ratio of the pair's co-change rate against the product of base rates (hypergeometric null). That controls for popularity, which is the failure recorded in row 153. Then require a named channel before the pair is promoted from data to advice: (a) data contract, an IDF-weighted vocabulary overlap or value-concordance certification between the two file sets that beats a per-repository null of random file pairs; (b) test-of, name kinship between a test node and its subject (the e2e and process boundary); (c) duplicated text between docs and code (shingled overlap). Data needed: history co-change (already in the model), the node graph (already read) and value-concordance indexes (already built). Cost: ~3-4 days, with the output additive in grain-advice/1 (an `evidence.channel` field). How we would know: re-run the node-cochange measurement on the four hand graphs plus Yggdrasil HEAD, and have a maintainer label the top 20 undeclared pairs as real or noise, with a pre-set bar of ≥60% real. A time split must also hold: pairs certified on history before T must predict co-change after T better than the popularity-matched control from row 153.

But row 153 says co-change partners are no better than popularity, and the advice contract deliberately keeps these pairs as data. This is speculative and 3-4 days of work, so low; do it after GM-7 lands.

title: Name the few imports that hold each cycle together (weighted minimum feedback arc set or agony), not just the cycle's members
where: Grain engine/relations.mjs:517-551 (Tarjan SCC, cycles as member lists), report.mjs moduleLayers; export `moduleGraph.cycles`
evidence: Yggdrasil's cached Grain model (.grain/cache/model.json, engine 0.4.0, built 2026-09-16) has a moduleGraph of 40 modules, 67 edges, and cycles of sizes [2, 3]. An exhaustive search for the minimum back-edge set per cycle gives: [source/cli/src/cli, source/cli/src/portal] with 16 imports inside the cycle, broken by 4 (portal→cli ×4); [core, relations, structure] with 38 imports, broken by 4 (relations→core ×2, structure→core ×2). At HEAD those edges are still there: grep finds `../cli/` imported in portal/engine-api.ts and `../core/` in relations/allowed-types.ts, relations/type-gate.ts, structure/observations.ts and structure/allowed-reads.ts. Grain today prints the members of each cycle only.
proposal: The math: for each SCC, find the minimum-weight feedback arc set, with weight = import count from moduleGraph edges. Solve it exactly by subset DP for SCCs up to ~15 nodes. Above that, use Tatti's agony (minimise Σ max(0, r(u)−r(v)+1)), which a min-cost circulation solves in polynomial time and which gives a layer rank as a by-product. Print 'this cycle is held by 4 of 16 imports: file:line…'. Say plainly that this is the smallest cut, not necessarily the right one. Data needed: file-level edges with lines (already in model.edges). Cost: ~1-2 days, pure. How we would know: replay history on corpus repositories that broke a cycle, and measure how often the edges maintainers actually removed fall inside the proposed cut, against a random-edge baseline. Secondary check: it must reproduce the 093 cycles exactly.

Because Yggdrasil 6.1.0 turns any undeclared dependency red (relation-undeclared-dependency, including TS type-only imports), a repository with a green check has a declared graph that is a superset of its code dependencies at node level. proposal: Per sampled interval, compute: nodes, edges/node, longest chain on the SCC condensation, SCC count and size, fan-in Gini, and the new edges that point upward against the previous interval's layer rank.
